correctness.rationale: A nonmember cell has precisely r_i+c_j neighbors in the fort; the absence of exactly-one pairs reduces to two quantified isolation/degree conditions. An exhaustive case split of row/column coverage forces four disjoint minimal incidence patterns; labeled-component EGFs, forests, and cycles give the exact polynomial. Universal proof steps and all edge cases were checked against the actual verifier, not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The 2015 maximal failed-zero-forcing result, restated in arXiv:2202.04997 Theorem 3.7, already implies minimum rook fort size four for factors of order at least four; this is prior-covered and not offered as a novelty claim. The assessed claim is the exhaustive four-class description and exact all-cardinality minimal-fort polynomial, neither entailed by the scalar extremal theorem nor by inspected Cartesian-product fort constructions and other graph-family counts.
residual_risks: Possible equivalent unindexed literature or an uncited exact enumeration of inclusion-maximal failed zero-forcing sets of rook graphs.

value.rationale: A complete minimal-fort hypergraph is the natural obstruction family to standard zero forcing, materially finer than a previously known minimum fort size. The novel four-case structural decomposition and finite coefficient formula count all inclusion-minimal obstructions, distinguish cycles from star covers and acyclic subdivisions, and have a plausible direct use in forcing transversal investigations.
